messageCenterItems.title: Power Apps - Information about SharePoint thumbnails not rendering
messageCenterItems.summary: We identified that changes made in relation to the retirement of SharePoint temporary authentication URLs communicated under MC1551122 may prevent thumbnails for SharePoint items from rendering in Power Apps.  How does this affect me?
messageCenterItems.body:
We identified that changes made in relation to the retirement of SharePoint temporary authentication URLs communicated under MC1551122 may prevent thumbnails for SharePoint items from rendering in Power Apps.

How does this affect me?
SharePoint thumbnails displayed in your apps may not render. Other app functionality is not as affected.

What action do I need to take?
To restore missing SharePoint thumbnails, republish the affected app. After the app is republished, users who start or restart it should see thumbnails render correctly within one hour. If your SharePoint thumbnails are rendering in Power Apps as expected, no action is required.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Up to 10-year recovery windows for SharePoint and OneDrive
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft 365 Backup now allows configurable recovery windows up to 10 years for SharePoint and OneDrive, extending from the previous 2 years. Administrators can set recovery periods from 3 months to 10 years, while Exchange backup windows remain unchanged. No action is needed unless longer retention is desired.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft 365 Backup now supports configurable recovery windows of up to 10 years for SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts, extending the previous maximum of two years. This update gives organizations greater flexibility to configure how long backup recovery points are retained.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Available now

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft 365 Backup for SharePoint and OneDrive

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Backup
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive for Business

What will happen

  • Administrators can configure recovery windows of 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 4 years, 5 years, 6 years, 7 years, 8 years, 9 years, or 10 years for SharePoint and OneDrive backup policies.
  • Exchange backup policies are unchanged. Supported recovery windows remain 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years.
  • The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies.
  • Weekly SharePoint and OneDrive recovery points beyond the previous 52-week horizon continue through the configured recovery window, up to 10 years.
  • Configuring a longer recovery window does not make 10 years of backup history immediately available.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required if your organization wants to keep its current recovery-window settings.

To configure a longer recovery window:

  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup.
  • Create a SharePoint or OneDrive backup policy and configure the Recovery window on the Backup Settings page or open an existing active policy and update its recovery window.
  • Select a supported recovery window of up to 10 years.
  • Review your settings and select Create policy or Update policy, as applicable.

We recommend that you:

  • Review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed.
  • Notify your backup administrators about the additional recovery-window options.
  • Update your internal documentation as appropriate.

Learn more

  • Create, view, and edit backup policies in Microsoft 365 Backup | Microsoft Learn
  • Overview of Microsoft 365 Backup | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

This update introduces longer configurable recovery windows for SharePoint and OneDrive backup policies. Organizations should review their applicable backup, data retention, and compliance requirements before configuring longer recovery windows.

messageCenterItems.title: OneDrive for Business:  Bug fixes to ensure proper storage quota aligns with license limits
messageCenterItems.summary: OneDrive for Business will fix a bug causing incorrect 1 TB storage quotas for users with certain license combinations. Starting January 2027, quotas will match the actual storage plan, potentially reducing some users' quotas. Organizations should review usage, adjust licenses, and prepare for possible read-only states.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

We're fixing an issue in OneDrive for Business license evaluation so that a user's OneDrive storage quota is determined by their applicable storage plan.

Today, users assigned certain storage-providing plans in combination with certain non-storage plans can incorrectly receive a 1 TB OneDrive quota. After this change, these combinations will no longer result in a 1 TB quota. OneDrive will instead apply the quota associated with the user's storage plan, which may be lower than 1 TB.

This change improves license and storage entitlement accuracy, helping organizations manage OneDrive capacity consistently with their assigned licenses.

Rollout Schedule:

Global: We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected: Your organization may be affected if users have a plan from both lists below.

Plans that provide OneDrive storage:

  • Deskless: 2 GB
  • Basic or Basic P3: 5 GB
  • Basic P2 or Plan 2A: 10 GB
  • OneDrive Clipchamp: 100 GB

Plans that don't provide OneDrive storage but, when combined with one of the plans above, can currently result in an incorrect 1 TB quota:

  • M365 Copilot SharePoint
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Stream
  • Microsoft Syntex Seat
  • Viva Amplify
  • Microsoft Clipchamp
  • Microsoft Clipchamp Premium
  • Viva Connections Premium

Users with these license-plan combinations are incorrectly assigned the standard 1 TB OneDrive quota instead of the storage allowance provided by their storage plan.

What will happen: OneDrive will correct how storage entitlement is determined for the license-plan combinations listed above. The user's OneDrive quota will instead reflect their applicable storage plan (as listed above). As a result, affected users who currently have a 1 TB quota will see their OneDrive storage quota decrease.

If an affected user is consuming more storage than their corrected license quota allows, their OneDrive will enter a read-only state. Users can reduce their stored content to bring their usage within their licensed quota. Organizations can also purchase additional storage using capacity packs.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  • Review OneDrive storage usage across your organization to identify users whose usage exceeds their licensed quota. See Identify OneDrive Users Over License-Based Storage Quota | PnP Samples and OneDrive site is read-only because storage quota was exceeded - SharePoint | Microsoft Learn.
  • Take corrective action for affected users: upgrade the user's license to increase available storage, or work with the user to reduce storage usage to within licensed limits.
  • Inform your helpdesk and SharePoint admins about this change so they can support users who may be placed into a read-only state.
  • If all users are within their licensed storage quotas, no action is required.

Additional resources: Add storage space, Site storage overquota enforcement FAQ.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
